headline.note: Documented work includes previously omitted private McDonald’s employment with unknown dates/hours. Remaining transitions and2002–2005 employment are unresolved. Neither headline total is calculable; unknown is not zero.

career_spells.employer: Office of the Hon. Stephen Martin MP (payroll entity unresolved)
career_spells.evidence_note: Her first speech says she moved to Stephen Martin's office after one and a half years at NSW Labor and describes electorate work as the next job. It does not state the appointment or cessation dates, payroll entity, hours or leave. Martin represented Macarthur and later Cunningham, but his service dates are not substituted for Byrnes's employment dates. Contemporary court record names Byrnes among four staff considered at a26March1996 Corrimal-office staffing meeting. This dates an employment observation, not commencement/cessation. Martin’s1999 thesis acknowledges her administrative/computing assistance; remuneration and whether nested staff duties are unknown. Court details of another employee’s salary, dismissal and contract are not transferred to Byrnes.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Office of the Hon. Sharon Bird MP (payroll entity unresolved)
career_spells.evidence_note: A legitimately public LinkedIn search result separates an executive-assistant role in 2005–2007 from the later adviser role. Byrnes's first speech independently confirms 17 years in Bird's electorate and ministerial offices, while ABC confirms she still worked for Bird in February 2022. Exact dates, payroll entity, hours and leave remain unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Commonwealth of Australia — Office of the Hon. Sharon Bird MP
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen official biography records senior policy and media adviser work from 2005 to 2022. The public LinkedIn result refines the senior role to July 2007–March 2022 and lists the prior executive-assistant position separately. Her first speech confirms work across Bird's electorate and ministerial offices but does not identify when office context, title or payroll changed. Hours, leave and any campaign break remain unresolved. In4September2023 speech she explicitly describes university study in her30s while a full-time adviser. This establishes full-time work during an undated subperiod, not the entire2007–2022 role. Calendar course boundaries and leave remain unknown; no dates calculated from age.24June2010 Bird parliamentary statement independently identifies Byrnes as her staffer organising work-experience visits. No transfer to Justine Elliot’s office inferred from visit. Primary2017FWC decision establishes Commonwealth MOP(S) employee status through named electorate-officer witness and personal payslip/account evidence;2018/2021Finance minutes independently identify Bird office. Generic electorate-officer classification coexists with profile adviser title, not a newly dated role transition. No whole-spell hours inferred.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official parliamentary and party biographies identify the qualification and institution. career_spells.employer: Australian Labor Party / Alison Byrnes federal election campaign (payroll entity unresolved)
career_spells.evidence_note: ABC reported Byrnes formally launching her Cunningham campaign on 25 February 2022 while still working for Sharon Bird. The AEC final results record her election on 21 May 2022. This is a bounded campaign-activity interval, not proof of a separate paid or full-time job. Preselection activity preceded the launch; its start, campaign remuneration, payroll entity, weekly hours, Bird-office leave/cessation and any March–May employment overlap remain unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Election candidacy and campaign activity are excluded under the codebook and are not added to the Bird staff spell or headline totals.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen roster and current official biographies establish House service from 21 May 2022. Committee or parliamentary duties are nested within this elected service.
career_spells.counting_note: Elected office is excluded under the codebook.
